output.one_liner: An open-source, self-hosted WordPress e-commerce platform providing REST API access for store management and integration with external systems.

auth.notes: REST API keys (consumer_key and consumer_secret pair) generated through WooCommerce admin panel; pages mention two authentication methods but only REST API keys are clearly detailed.

evidence.snippet: The WooCommerce REST API uses a key system to control access. Each set of keys is linked to a WordPress user on your site.
WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API. It is also possible to authenticate using any WP REST API authentication plugin or method.

access.notes: WooCommerce is free, open-source software that can be self-hosted. API keys are generated through the WooCommerce admin panel without vendor approval.

evidence.snippet: WooCommerce is the free, Open Source ecommerce platform for WordPress.
To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user: Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. Select Create an API key
This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods and standard HTTP verbs
Webhooks Topics Visual interface Webhook properties Create a webhook Retrieve a webhook List all webhooks
Use the REST API for store management data. Use the Store API for shopper-facing product, cart, and checkout flows.
WooCommerce MCP Connect a compatible AI client to a running store through the WordPress MCP Adapter and WooCommerce abilities.
WooCommerce registers product and order abilities that compatible AI clients can use through the WordPress MCP Adapter. This integration is a developer preview.

buildability.rationale: Free, open-source REST API with self-serve credential generation and no approval requirements.

overview_evidence.snippet: The WooCommerce REST API connects your store to external systems and services.
WooCommerce is the free, Open Source ecommerce platform for WordPress.
WooCommerce (WC) 2.6+ is fully integrated with the WordPress REST API.

unknown_reasons.auth: Second authentication method mentioned but not specified; references WP REST API authentication plugins which may include OAuth or bearer tokens.
